trust_decision.summary: Savon::Model decides at method-definition time that a WSDL operation name is Ruby source rather than data: the name is interpolated into a module_eval string at lib/savon/model.rb:31-35 (class methods) and lib/savon/model.rb:40-44 (instance methods), so a name containing newlines/backticks closes the generated `def` and executes code in the application process.

landing_point.why: The summary names the .all_operations class method over WSDL operation names; .all_operations (lib/savon/model.rb:23-25) delegates to .operations (lib/savon/model.rb:16-21), which calls define_class_operation, whose module_eval at lib/savon/model.rb:31 is the first eval sink a reader meets.

fix_sites.entry_point: Savon::Model.all_operations / Savon::Model.operations -> generated class-level SOAP operation method
fix_sites.module_kind: public DSL mixin (Savon::Model extended into user model classes) generating methods in class_operation_module

fix_sites.entry_point: Savon::Model.all_operations / Savon::Model.operations -> generated instance-level SOAP operation method
fix_sites.module_kind: generated instance module (instance_operation_module) mixed into the model class

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory write-up names only '.all_operations' and the class-level methods, and the second code-generation site (define_instance_operation, lib/savon/model.rb:39-45) sits in a generated instance module that a solver can call the same mechanism already handled by the class-method fix; likewise the advisory says operation names passed to '.operations' are trusted, so a solver may leave that route unserialised.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Generated method names must stay snakecased (WSDL 'GetTiCs' -> :get_ti_cs) while the original operation object (a Symbol) must still be handed unchanged to client.call, which raises unless the name is a Symbol; the pinned code preserved this via StringUtils.snakecase for the def name and '#{operation.inspect}' for the argument. A fix that defines the method under operation.to_s, or calls client.call with the snakecased name, breaks .all_operations on real WSDL names. The two existing source_location specs (spec/savon/model_spec.rb:109-131) additionally pin the generated method's reported location into model.rb.

O6_input_shapes: String operation name containing newlines, backticks, quotes and 'end'/'def' text (WSDL-supplied)
same name interpolated twice in the instance-method site: once as the method name and once as the receiver call in the body (lib/savon/model.rb:41-42)
Symbol operation names passed through '.operations :authenticate' that must remain Symbols for client.call
non-String operation objects whose to_s/inspect is attacker-influenced (the pinned code interpolated operation.inspect at lib/savon/model.rb:33; the fix passes the object through untouched)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a filtered/renamed registration route such as '.operations(only:/rename:)' or '.operations_from_wsdl' that feeds names from a config file or a previously fetched WSDL into the same code generator
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already separates the name source (.all_operations) from the definition API (.operations), so adding a filter/rename option that reuses the same generation helper is a natural maintainer feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third generated-module builder in class_operation_module/instance_operation_module that derives extra helper methods (e.g. 'authenticate!') from the same operation names
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: two near-identical generated Module builders already exist here; a maintainer adding a convenience variant that wraps the same module_eval is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the test DSL generating one helper method per declared expectation name (e.g. 'def expect_authenticate') via string eval
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: spec-helper DSLs commonly generate one method per declared name, and this Interface already turns a caller-supplied name into stored state.

O9_family: code injection via dynamic evaluation of attacker-controlled names (CWE-94); no denial-of-service component

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby >= 3.0, Bundler, Rake ('bundle exec rake' -> RSpec 3.9); gems: akami, builder, gyoku, httpi, mail, nokogiri, nori, wasabi, faraday, puma/rack, mocha, simplecov
services: spec/savon/model_spec.rb starts an in-process Puma HTTP server on localhost:17172 (spec/integration/support/server.rb:31-40); no external service needed
O10_build.project_tests: spec/savon/model_spec.rb covers .operations, .all_operations, class- and instance-level method generation, source_location, override-with-super and (added by the fix) the malicious-WSDL case; uses local fixtures spec/fixtures/wsdl/*.xml

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Keep module_eval but escape or strip the dangerous characters in the operation name (or wrap the name in a sanitizer regex), which leaves the second interpolation position in the instance-method body (lib/savon/model.rb:42) and the eval sink itself in place.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/savon/options.rb:34-38 dispatches with send(option, value) on caller-supplied option keys, a separate dynamic-dispatch sink not covered by this advisory's operation-name protection; noted only, not pursued.
